entities.name: San Antonio-class amphibious transport dock
entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
The San Antonio-class amphibious transport dock (LPD) represents a significant evolution in naval warfare capability, first commissioned in 2003 as part of the U.S. Navy's efforts to enhance amphibious assault operations. This class is named after the city of San Antonio, Texas, and is designed to support a range of military operations, from traditional amphibious assaults to humanitarian missions. The class comprises several vessels, including USS San Antonio (LPD 17), the lead ship, and includes notable features such as a well deck for landing craft, a flight deck for helicopters, and accommodations for a large contingent of Marines and their equipment.

The San Antonio-class LPDs were developed in response to the changing nature of warfare in the 21st century, where rapid response and versatility became crucial. The first ship, USS San Antonio, was commissioned on January 14, 2006, and since then, the class has participated in numerous operations, including Joint Task Force operations and humanitarian assistance missions following natural disasters. The design incorporates advanced technology and enhanced survivability features, allowing these ships to operate effectively in contested environments. The class has served as a platform for deploying Marine Expeditionary Units (MEUs) and played a pivotal role in operations across the globe, including deployments to the Persian Gulf and support during the Haiti earthquake in 2010.
